the linear dependence between particle number concentration at the 3–6 nm and sulphuric acids observed in field measurements is due to: (1) the low growth rate of particles from 1 to 3 nm; (2) the assumed size for nucleated clusters; and (3) the assumed nucleation mechanism.

the observed linear dependence between the 3–6-nm particle number concentration and sulphuric concentration may be reproduced in model simulations by using activation nucleation mechanism with a low saturation pressure for the condensing organic vapours.

the sulphuric-acid dependence of new particle formation is affected by: (1) the assumed size for nucleation, (2) the assumed growth rate of the clusters between 1 and ~3 nm, (3) the assumed nucleation mechanism and (4) the assumed saturation vapour pressure of condensable organic compounds.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the observed linear or square dependence between particle number at 3–5 nm and sulphur acid can be explained with the activation nucleation mechanism with low saturation vapour pressures of the condensable vapour.
the observed sulphuric acid dependency at the 3–6-nm size range is not a clear indication of the nucleation mechanism, but it is a result of the growth rate from 1 to 3 nm.

the observed linear dependence of the particle number concentration on sulphuric acids is not an unambiguous proof for the ternary nucleation mechanism, and the linear dependence could be achieved also with activation or kinetic mechanism.

the sulphuric-acid dependence of particle concentration is very sensitive to the assumed nucleation mechanism and to the size at which nucleation takes place.
